origin_result.basis: The product requires a change in tariff sub-heading (CTSH) and a regional value content of at least 40% (VA 40%). A 6-digit HS code is needed for non-originating Emollients (BOM row 2) to complete the verification.

procedure.step: The factory must be registered outside a free zone through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service before applying for a certificate of origin.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for the certificate using the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service provided by the Ministry of Foreign Trade, uploading factory registration proof and commercial invoices.
Pay the certificate of origin fee of AED 50 charged by the Ministry of Foreign Trade for shipments with an invoice value up to AED 100,000.
The competent authority issues the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within five working days of exportation, valid for 12 months for a single import.

The Indian importer claims preferential tariff treatment upon filing the bill of entry and must maintain supporting origin information; electronic certificates are reportedly accepted via e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).
The exporter must maintain all origin documents and cost breakdowns for at least five years from the end of the year of certificate issuance.

caveats.note: The '+' symbol in the product-specific rule is interpreted by Mansha as 'and', requiring both CTSH and VA 40% tests to pass.
Duty savings are estimated based on the shipment value provided; India charges customs duty on the CIF assessable value at import, and CEPA rate reductions apply to Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which requires the factory to be located outside a free zone.
